question: The growing demand for long-term care is a social challenge for Europe. According to the Italian statistics institute (ISTAT), more than 12 million people in Italy provide care for free, and 4.4 million of them live with the person they are caring for, with women most affected (21.7 %, compared with 17 % of men)1.

A report by Italy’s National Council of Economy and Labour (CNEL) on the social value of carers shows that more than half associate care with emotional and psychological stress2. In Sicily and southern Italy, the critical nature of local services and disparities in access to care exacerbate the family burden.

Sicily has recently allocated more than EUR 2 million to district social and health services for the ‘caregiver bonus’, confirming the need for structural measures3. The European Care Strategy and the 2022 Council Recommendation call for accessible and high-quality services, support for informal carers and a reduction in territorial inequalities4.
In addition, Directive (EU) 2019/1158 protects reconciliation, leave and work flexibility, with a view to ensuring gender equality5. In view of the above: 1.

Does the Commission intend to monitor the implementation of the European Care Strategy in Italy with a view to reducing territorial inequalities in access to care and support services for family carers in Sicily and southern Italy? If so, how?

Will it mobilise the ESF+, ERDF and other cohesion policy instruments to increase investment in home services and psychological support for family carers, especially in regions that lack care services?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.11.2026) The European Care Strategy1 and the Council Recommendation on access to affordable, highquality long-term care (LTC)2 provide a framework to improve access to care services and support informal carers, including through counselling, psychological support and respite care.
All Member States shared national implementation plans3, and the Commission monitors relevant developments through an indicator-based Monitoring Framework4, feeding into the European Semester5.

The European Social Fund Plus (ESF+) and the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF) support investments in LTC services and infrastructure, with national and regional authorities responsible for selecting and implementing projects, and the Commission for monitoring implementation.

Sicily's 2021–2027 programmes include measures to strengthen proximity social services, integrated care and territorial healthcare services6,7. The ESF+ can support home-based services and psychological assistance for informal carers, while the ERDF can finance related infrastructure, subject to programme priorities.

The Recovery and Resilience Facility has supported reforms and investments under Italy’s National Recovery and Resilience Plan to strengthen long-term care, home-based services and independent living for older people and people with disabilities. The Commission will prepare a report for the Council on the implementation of the LTC Recommendation in 2027.
The President of the Commission announced in her 2026 State of the Union address8 that in 2027, the Commission will launch a European Care Deal to address demographic and care challenges.
